seed.description: A base resolved by bare name needs a local ref, and a sha:refs/heads push creates only the remote one

A construct-scoped assert extracted from norm()-joined text silently yields '', and a scratch-deletion proof whose literal wraps across a source line is a no-op — either one turns a both-ways proof into theatre
A defect inside an error-suppressed fail-open step degrades to silent inaction, so rate it by where the failure routes, not by the defect alone
Assert a config switch is in its legal set and check the shipped value once at review, or a later config-only flip turns the guard red
To prove every call goes through one wrapper, count the call sites in the source and require that they all sit inside the wrapper
A diff guard must read .gitmodules at the diff refs with git config --blob, not from the working tree
A shell loop that walks up with dirname and stops only at / never ends on a relative path; add a progress guard
A boto3 helper that returns None or False on every ClientError makes throttles, 5xx and denials look like a missing object
A digit check and [ -lt ] accept 08, but $((08)) fails as octal, so normalize once with $((10#$v)) after validation
A violation fixture checked by rule id proves the rule fired, not that each banned pattern fires, so add one row per pattern by spawning eslint on a virtual path
A never-raises entrypoint needs a degraded sentinel or non-zero exit for an item-level failure, and must resolve its status output location first
A test that exactly one entry holds some keys must collect (name, keys) pairs in a list and count the quoted key in the file text
A leaked semaphore permit lowers the peak instead of raising it, so a peak-only assertion passes; also assert the counter drains after rejected dispatches
A git command spelled in an agent prompt needs a test that runs that exact text through bash
Delete the feature in your head or by mutation; every assertion that names it must go red, or the test proves only no crash
A test that never goes red for the current code, or does not discriminate alone, can still be a valid guard; check for future-regression intent and sibling tests first
A token or count assertion over a broad text region passes on other text in that region, so scope it to the item's own span
A trailer set as its own paragraph is lost once an agent appends a Co-Authored-By paragraph
A sandbox probe must use git -C <sandbox> on every call, because the shell tool resets cwd between calls and a bare git push hits the real remote
A rotated API token dies at once only if the AppSync Lambda authorizer ttlOverride and the stack resultsCacheTtl are both zero.
Pair every absence assert with a positive control that proves the collector could see the thing, or it passes vacuously
A relative-path ancestor-walk test false-allows when its cwd holds the marker, so run it from a verified marker-free directory
A new early-exit guard makes old 'nothing written' assertions pass because the guard refuses first, so re-aim each fixture at the guarded branch
An AST one-home guard must flag every Load-context name, attribute and ImportFrom of the helper, not only ast.Call
In a bash case pattern, * matches / too, so a glob is not a path anchor and **/ is not globstar; fences need a '..' check and an absolute arm, file conventions need a root plus nested pair
A bash 3.2 watchdog around one call inside $(...) needs detached stdio, an empty pid seed and an expired gate on exit 143
A test can expire a bash script's SECONDS deadline by exporting SECONDS, but it reaches only the pre-check arms
A CDK custom IEcsLaunchTarget that returns a CapacityProviderStrategy renders no LaunchType, and Chain.custom binds a caller's next() to every end state
A large CDK stack can hit CloudFormation's 500-resource limit, so pin each stack to a resource budget in a unit test and move monitors to a sibling stack for headroom
A checked-in comment or docstring that cites a private note id gives a repo reader no way to resolve it
Push first, then advance the local ref only after ls-remote confirms; classify a lost push by the [rejected] token, never by non-fast-forward
CloudWatch Logs caps metric filters at 100 per log group and will not raise it, so pin a per-log-group filter count in a test
Read a Cognito caller's GitHub login from the identities claim, never from the user-writable preferred_username.
for m in $(cmd) and dirname \"$(cmd)\" both hide a failed cmd, so capture it first with x=$(cmd) && and check it
A composer that clears its draft only after the write resolves sends twice on a double tap unless it guards the pending post.
Container Insights family metrics are one datapoint per task per minute: use Sum or SampleCount, never Average
A cross-process request_hash test runs children under distinct PYTHONHASHSEED values with a timeout and expects the job_name to differ
A hand-written fake DynamoDB table in unit tests accepts bare reserved-word attribute paths that live DynamoDB rejects
A die() helper that calls process.exit inside a try block skips the enclosing finally, so scratch dirs leak on every error path; throw a tagged Error and exit only in main()
A bare git status hash misses a second edit to a dirty file, so fingerprint blob hashes from a -z status
A DynamoDB conditional claim that treats an absent or NULL attribute as free must use attribute_type(..., NULL), not an equality test
A proof of absence built on command output passes on a command error when stderr and exit status are swallowed (2>/dev/null || true, or grep -c over a failed producer)
A test matrix written from natural examples misses the boundary cells, so list every cell and give each AND'd condition its own negative test
ESLint flat-config import-ban blocks replace earlier rule options, so each subset block repeats its parent zones and exemptions go in ignores.
expo-router useFocusEffect re-runs its callback on every identity change while the route is focused, so a callback that depends on loaded data can clear a navigation latch.
A failed git worktree add followed by cd does not stop a compound shell command, so the rest runs in the original checkout
Find the merge commit that brought in a branch tip by walking rev-list --first-parent --merges tip..target, never the whole history

Treat a review finding's fix text as a floor: sweep every sibling site of the same rule, bind restated values with a pin, and extract on the second copy, or the next review round finds the mirror case
A fork-per-item parallel helper copies static_args dicts, so child mutations never reach parent or siblings; it also has a pipe contract and a test seam
In a forked-process test, an assert on the child's behavior needs a control that ran in the child
The git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir main-checkout anchor needs capture-then-check, and its probe succeeds inside a bare repo
git diff --name-only prints only a rename's destination, so a footprint check needs --no-renames
A plain git pathspec resolves against the current directory, but git show <rev>:<path> is top-of-tree, so a script using one repo-root path for both needs :(top) on the pathspec
An unconditional git probe in a previously git-free hook makes every test fixture root need to live outside any git working tree
git revert --no-commit skips the dirty-index refusal, so staged content rides into the revert commit
Under pipefail, `cmd | grep -Fxq` can SIGPIPE cmd on large output, so the pipeline returns 141 and an if-caller reads no match
Turning a raise into an in-handler degrade forfeits the Step Functions retry ladder, so a transient fault longer than the handler's own backoff budget drops data
From Jest 30, a failures-only agent reporter replaces the default under AI-agent env vars, so a log lists no passing suite paths unless the reporter is pinned.
The jest-expo preset sets passWithNoTests, so a path-filtered jest check passes with no test file until jest.config.js overrides it.
A hook that reads a key with jq // empty and gates on non-empty lets a present empty, null, false or array value pass

A Lambda layer bundler that packs one layer folder alone ships a symlink to a sibling layer as a dangling link, so share a module by placing its one copy in a layer the functions already attach; container-image functions need a symlink per shared module
Lambda layers bundled with a native pip on an arm64 build host ship aarch64 wheels to x86_64 Lambdas; cross-install for the declared architecture
A Lambda retryAttempts setting applies only to async invokes; Step Functions invokes synchronously, so only its Retry blocks retry
Read an Anthropic response's text from the first type=='text' block, not content[0]; positional content[0]['text'] readers break on thinking-first replies

CloudWatch Logs Insights StartQuery rejects the dashboard widget form's SOURCE prefix and a query that opens with a pipe, so run any printed query through StartQuery once before a runbook depends on it
To test a single git failure arm, put a git wrapper first on PATH that exits 128 for the exact call and delegates every other call
Mechanical tag sweep can corrupt backtick tokens in // comments
Moving explicitly named CloudWatch monitors to another stack deletes before it creates, which loses a metric window and resets alarm state
A negative-grep drift guard can trip on a prose comment with the same literal; reword the comment, keep the guard
A test that no fixture fires a degrade token must call the guard's own functions in the shared harness and opt in per token
A bare-equality Node ESM run-as-CLI guard silently no-ops under symlink invocation, so realpath argv[1] before comparing
Normalize an args input by parsing it when it is a string, then guard that the result is a non-null object, because a try/catch alone lets null and scalars through
A module with an optional fast dependency and a pure-Python fallback silently runs the slow fallback on a Lambda layer that omits the dependency, and no test forces that path
A `func || true` under set -e hides real write failures inside func, so the script can report false success
When a spec says no other keys change, pin the whole key set with ==, because a presence check lets an extra key leak in
Plain git check-ignore reads the index, so a hook walk that mirrors ripgrep skips must ask with --no-index
A plan's claims about the source system of a port are often wrong, so capture fixtures from the deployed commit
printf-interpolated JSON payloads make embedded-quote test cases vacuous
A test that names a path must prove that path ran with an effect only it produces, such as an injection hook's fired record or a log line only that branch writes
Push after PR merge recreates dead branch, misses PR
A module-level import between two test files can pass the gate on collection order alone, and each file's own task check command misses it
Stub heavy third-party deps into sys.modules via monkeypatch.setitem, not a bare assignment, or the stub leaks past the test into later by-path handler imports in the same pytest session
A read-only git call in a live worktree can write its index or run core.fsmonitor, so pass GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 and -c core.fsmonitor=false
A README de-mirror guard intersects backticked spans with module constants read by AST
An LLM reply that answers per numbered item needs max_tokens sized to the item count, not a fixed 1024
Remove the worktree that has a branch checked out before deleting the branch, and let the delete fail loud
Flipping a default or superseding a decision fixes one doc surface and strands the rest, so sweep all surfaces and assert the old value is absent
A per-call poll budget holds for one call; a fan-out helper with cap P runs N calls in ceil(N/P) waves
Without s3:ListBucket, GetObject on a missing key returns 403 AccessDenied, not 404, so an absent-code allowlist never matches
A handler that fetches items one at a time can pass its timeout only on a retry, because per-type checkpoints shrink each attempt; fan the fetch out and add a retry
A Step Functions Catch landing past a Parameters-rebuilding Pass with no ResultPath silently drops any key that Pass omits
A leading MaxAttempts: 0 retrier makes Catch fire at once, ahead of a later States.ALL retrier
A per-site swap to a new shared function goes shadow, then bake, then cleanup; gate the bake on a log MetricFilter
A shared-deadline regression passes vacuously if stage one is served at once, so make stage one spend part of the budget
Falling back to {} on a failed read before rewriting a shared JSON blob silently deletes the keys other writers own
A `[0-9]+`-only grep/sed extraction of a JS numeric value truncates 100_000, 0x13880 and 1e5, so a ceiling-raise check can fail open
Shell tests of an env-var-triggered code path must unset that var before pre-existing fixture cases — an ambient developer/CI export silently activates it
Never-raises handlers: split log tokens by meaning, keep them non-substring for MetricFilters, mirror the constants across files
A Lambda handler that ignores the table env the stack passes works only while the stack keeps fixed table names.
A binary truncated/ok classifier over an LLM finish_reason maps refusals and content filters to 'ok', so a retry keyed on 'ok' misses them
A stranded remote tip makes `git branch -d` refuse a local branch that IS merged — unset the upstream, don't escalate to -D
Moving or renaming a file in a shared-library submodule leaves superproject symlinks to it dangling until the submodule bump commit retargets them
A sweep for callers of a shared-library helper that covers only the library missed a superproject test passing the removed parameter, so the submodule bump broke it
A submodule working tree can lag the commit the superproject pins, so read submodule code with git show at the pinned SHA
A trailing-newline deny row in a command guard can never pass; the real bypass is an interior newline joining two commands
Piping a newline-joined path list through xargs splits on every space, so iterate with while IFS= read -r instead
In zsh, an unbraced $T:path in a git <rev>:<path> argument triggers parameter modifiers (:h, :s) and mangles the path; write \"${T}:path\"
